pValue.name: exact p-value
pValue.definition: Exact two-sided sign-flip test: the share of all 2^n sign patterns of the per-task differences whose mean is at least as far from zero as the observed one.
pValue.denominator: Denominator: all 2^n sign vectors over the n tasks of the primary condition; the task is the unit, so trials of one task never count as separate wins.

mde.name: minimal detectable effect
mde.definition: Minimal detectable effect in pp = (t(0.975, n-1) + t(0.8, n-1)) x SD_d / sqrt(n): the smallest release effect this design detects with 80% power at alpha 0.05.
mde.denominator: Denominator: sqrt(n) over the n tasks; SD_d is the spread of per-task differences, an assumed 0.30 until an A/A run measures it.

costPerSuccess.name: cost per verified success
costPerSuccess.definition: Sum of the cost of every physical attempt at pinned prices, over all assigned slots of the arm, failed runs included.
costPerSuccess.denominator: Denominator: verified successes, runs whose hidden verifier passed under the clean regrade with no veto gate fired.

add.hiddenNote: Hidden tests, reference solutions and controls never appear in this UI. The page shows counts and pass or fail only.
add.copyFailedAnnounce: Could not copy: select the command and copy it by hand

task.init: Once per company: scaffold a project folder with its config, an agents folder and a benchmarks folder.
task.taskInit: Cut a task from a fix commit: repo/ is the tree at -base, the reference diff and the new tests come from -reference and are hidden.
task.edit: Rewrite the instruction in your own words. Validation fails while the EDIT ME marker is still there.
task.validate: Check the task. Review the hidden tests it prints: tests written beside a fix can encode the implementation.
task.admit: Prove the verifier is fair: reference passes 3 times, empty and mutants fail, null agents and the exploit fail, no secrets, no network.

suite.init: Start a suite from a template: python-pytest, node-test, go-test or generic-reward.
suite.image: Put your toolchain in the suite's base image. The verifier runs in it with no network.
suite.verifier: Say how the verifier reports: junit (default), reward with a threshold, or exit_code.
suite.lock: Lock the suite, then admit every task. Only admitted tasks can be planned.

agent.init: Describe your agent in one YAML file: command, python or http-service (LangGraph, FastAPI, an Agents SDK app).
agent.build: Build its image. With build.base_arg it is built once per suite on that suite's base image.
agent.check: Conformance check that costs nothing: one task against the scripted model, PASS, WARN or FAIL per row.
agent.contract: Your agent only has to send its model calls to the URL and key it is given. No SDK.

imported.title: Imported from
imported.description: Written by bifrost-bench import from a local copy of a public benchmark. The upstream data is not committed, and each task counts only after its own admission passes here.
imported.label: Import record

scenario.title: Scenario
scenario.hint: What runs beside the agent and what the verifier reads.
scenario.imageHint: The task brings its own image instead of the suite's base image and a repo folder.
scenario.buildNetwork: network during the image build only
scenario.servicesHint: Started beside the agent, after the suite's services, on a network no other run can reach. Environment values and seed files stay on the server.
scenario.proxiedHint: The agent's calls pass the per-run tool proxy, which records them and can inject faults.
scenario.hiddenHint: Only the verifier and other services reach it.
scenario.sessionsHint: Each session is a fresh agent process, run in this order. Only the last session's output is graded.
scenario.persists: Carried between sessions: the /memory volume and the agent's own memory paths. Nothing else, unless a session keeps the workspace.
scenario.resetsWorkspace: workspace reset to the starting state
scenario.artifactsHint: Files the agent must leave in the workspace. After the run each match is copied to artifacts/<id>/ in the run folder, sealed, and read by the verifier.
scenario.skillsHint: Installed in the agent's skills folder, unless the run turns skills off.
scenario.impossibleBody: Its tests contradict its instruction, so no honest solution exists. A pass can only come from cheating, such as editing the tests or special-casing the checks, and the impossible_pass gate records it as an integrity violation.

suiteHealth.title: Suite health
suiteHealth.description: Read from sealed runs across experiments. A flaky verifier corrupts verdicts and is a defect; agent variance is normal and is shown apart from it.

reason.no_store: The server has no run store, so health cannot be read from sealed runs.
reason.not_found: The server has no health report for this suite.

suiteHealth.computed: Computed {{when}} from {{runs}} sealed runs across {{experiments}} experiments.
suiteHealth.thresholds: Difficulty is labelled after {{minRuns}} scored runs from {{minConfigs}} agent configs: easy at or above a {{easy}} pass rate, hard at or below {{hard}}. Intervals are Wilson score intervals at {{level}}. Infra trouble means infra failures above {{infra}}; timeouts means timeouts above {{timeout}}.

stats.label: Suite health counts
stats.heldOutHint: Tasks whose instruction and files are not served.
stats.quarantinedHint: Tasks kept out of new plans.

suiteHealth.noFlags: No task carries a health flag.

flagHints.flaky_verifier: The verifier graded the same output differently, or the reference did not always pass. Verdicts on this task are not trustworthy.
flagHints.difficulty_mismatch: Observed difficulty differs from the declared one.
flagHints.no_discrimination: Every agent config always passes, or always fails: the task says nothing about which agent is better.
flagHints.saturated: Every scored run of every agent config passed.
flagHints.dead: Every scored run of every agent config failed.
flagHints.timeouts: Agents hit the wall-time cap more often than the threshold.
flagHints.insufficient_data: Too few scored runs or agent configs to label difficulty.

suiteHealth.noRunsHint: No sealed run of this task was found.
suiteHealth.varianceHint: How often the same agent config both passed and failed. Normal for agents, not a task defect.
suiteHealth.heldOutHint: Held-out task: its instruction and files are not served (server config held_out.visible is false).
suiteHealth.heldOutVisibleHint: Held-out task, shown because the server config sets held_out.visible.
suiteHealth.heldOutRow: Title, files and checks are withheld for a held-out task.

board.toggleHint: Show the separate board of held-out tasks. The public board never counts a held-out task.
board.bannerHint: Scores from held-out tasks only, from experiments that selected them. They are never mixed into the public board.

quarantine.hint: Kept out of new plans since {{when}} ({{source}}): {{reason}}

detail.title: Health
detail.noRuns: No sealed run of this task was found, so there is no health to show yet.
detail.quarantineBody: Kept out of new plans. Results already recorded stay valid.
detail.flakyBody_one: Flaky verifier: {{count}} piece of evidence from {{checks}} checks. Verdicts on this task are not trustworthy until the verifier is fixed.
detail.flakyBody_other: Flaky verifier: {{count}} pieces of evidence from {{checks}} checks. Verdicts on this task are not trustworthy until the verifier is fixed.
detail.verifierUnchecked: Nothing could have shown a flaky verifier yet: no regrades, repeated outputs, oracle runs or reference repeats.

discrimination.always_pass: No information: every agent config always passes.
discrimination.always_fail: No information: every agent config always fails.
discrimination.single_config: Only one agent config ran, so there is nothing to separate.

detail.varianceBody: How often the same agent config both passed and failed across trials. This is ordinary agent behavior, not a defect of the task or its verifier.
detail.varianceNone: No agent config has scored trials yet.

agents.title: Agents
agents.subtitle: Every agent config in agents/: the system under test. Anything that runs in a container, edits the workspace and sends its model calls through Bifrost can be benchmarked.
agents.synthetic: Synthetic fixture data. These agent configs are examples for checking the screen.
agents.loadError: Could not load the agent configs.
agents.empty: No agent configs yet. Run `bifrost-bench agent init <id> -template command`.
agents.secretNote: Environment values are never shown, only variable names. Delivered files are listed by path, never by content.
agents.label: Agent configs
agents.perSuiteHint: build.base_arg is set: the image is built once per suite on that suite's base image.
agents.evidenceGatewayHint: No parser: success, steps, tokens, cost and time come from Bifrost's rows for the run's key.
agents.modelHint: A placeholder: every experiment sets the model, and an arm may vary it.
agents.scriptedHint: A scripted control agent, used by admission and dry runs. Its runs are not findings.
agents.runsHint: Sealed runs of this config id in any experiment, including dry runs against the scripted model. The leaderboard separates live from synthetic.

track.label: Track
track.codingHint: Edit a repository; hidden tests decide.
track.terminalHint: Work in a whole container; its state is checked afterwards.
track.tool_useHint: Call tools against a service; the final state is checked.
track.mcpHint: Tools reached over the Model Context Protocol.
track.memoryHint: Several sessions; recall is checked in the last one.
track.skillsHint: The same task with and without agent skills.
track.safetyHint: Attacks delivered through tool results or files.
track.qaHint: A written answer, matched or judged.
track.browserHint: A web application operated through a browser; its final state is checked.
track.computer_useHint: A desktop operated through screenshots, mouse and keyboard; its final state is checked.
track.artifactHint: Produce files, such as a report, a chart or a model, graded on their content.
track.otherHint: A track this version of the UI does not know.

grading.label: Grading
grading.verifiedHint: A deterministic check decides every outcome. No model grades.
grading.judgedHint: A pinned judge model decides each outcome, not a deterministic check. Judged results are never compared with verified ones.
grading.judgedBody: In this suite a judge model decides whether each answer is correct. The model, its prompt version and its number of votes are pinned in suite.yaml and hashed into every manifest, and its cost is reported apart from the agent's. Results here are never ranked against, or compared with, a verified suite.

output.label: Output
output.diffHint: The verifier reads the agent's workspace patch.
output.answerHint: The verifier reads the answer the agent wrote.
output.stateHint: The verifier reads files exported from the services after the run.
output.artifactHint: The verifier reads files the agent left in the workspace, copied out and sealed after the run.

imports.title: Imports
imports.subtitle: Public benchmarks this bench can turn into suites. An importer reads a local copy of the upstream data and writes an ordinary suite; nothing upstream is committed.
imports.synthetic: Synthetic fixture data. These importers are examples for checking the screen, not what this server links.
imports.label: Importers
imports.untrusted: Upstream data is untrusted input: it is read as data, never run on this machine, and an imported task counts only after its own reference passes and its empty control fails here.
imports.licenseVaries: varies per task: check each task's provenance

workers.title: Workers
workers.subtitle: Other machines that lease slots from this server, run them with the normal pipeline, and upload sealed run folders. This server keeps the spend cap and the lease table.
workers.synthetic: Synthetic fixture data. These workers are examples for checking the screen.
workers.offBody: The worker API is off unless the server starts with BENCH_WORKER_TOKEN set, so every run happens on this machine.
workers.offHow: To add a worker, set BENCH_WORKER_TOKEN on the server, then on the other machine (same project, same commit, its own stack):
workers.empty: The worker API is on, but no worker has registered yet.
workers.label: Remote workers

states.idleHint: Registered and waiting for a slot.
states.lostHint: Stopped answering; its leases go back to the queue.

trends.title: Trends
trends.subtitle: Each agent config lineage (agent and model) over experiments, one point per config hash. A slow regression shows here even when no single release verdict caught it.
trends.empty_one: Only {{count}} point matches these filters. A trend needs at least 2 points to draw a line.
trends.empty_other: {{count}} points match these filters. A trend needs at least 2 points to draw a line.

syntheticHint.exclude: Live runs only. Scripted agents and the scripted model are left out.
syntheticHint.only: Scripted agent or scripted model runs only. Their numbers are not findings.

lineages.title: Latest change per lineage
lineages.description: Newest point against the one before it, by the exact sign-flip test on the tasks both ran (alpha {{alpha}}). Too few tasks says cannot tell, never regressed.

chart.title: {{metric}} over time
chart.description: One line per lineage. A gap means the metric was not observed for that point.
chart.noValues: No point has a value for this metric.
chart.legendConfigChanged: Diamond: config hash changed from the previous point
chart.legendRelease: Red ring: release verdict regressed or blocked
chart.legendInterval: Bar: descriptive 95% interval over task success rates

table.title: Every point
table.description: The chart's numbers. Medians per run for tokens and wall time; false completion is a share of runs.
table.caption: Trend points by lineage, oldest first

footnote.source: Read from the results index, which is derived from sealed run folders and can be rebuilt at any time. A trend is a monitoring signal; release verdicts, the leaderboard and releases read the sealed files, never this index.
footnote.rejected_one: {{count}} run is listed as rejected because its seal did not verify. It is never charted.
footnote.rejected_other: {{count}} runs are listed as rejected because their seals did not verify. They are never charted.

review.title: Human review
review.subtitle: Runs a person should look at: split or unparsable judge votes, undecided graders, fired veto gates, false completions and flags. A review is a hash-chained record beside the sealed run. It never edits sealed evidence and changes results only where an analysis asks for grade source reviewed.
review.noExperiments: No experiment yet. Run one first; its runs that need a person show up here.

queue.title: Queue
queue.description: Sealed runs whose grade a person should check, with the outcome in effect under grade source reviewed.
queue.loadError: Could not load the review queue.
queue.empty: No run of this experiment needs review.
queue.emptyFiltered: No run of this experiment has this reason.
queue.problemsHint: Reviews that failed their hash, chain or parent seal check are ignored, and runs whose seal does not verify are left out. Nothing here changes a result.

decisionHint.pass: The run succeeded. Also overrules a veto gate that fired. Counts as 1, at evidence level reviewed.
decisionHint.fail: The run did not succeed. Counts as 0.
decisionHint.invalid: The evidence cannot decide, for example a broken judge or verifier. Counts as unknown.
decisionHint.flag_only: Records a concern for someone else to look at. The outcome stays as it is.

panel.title: Run {{id}}
panel.select: Pick a run in the queue to see its evidence and record a review.

timeline.title: Reviews
timeline.description: Every valid review of this run in log order, oldest first. A later decision supersedes an earlier one; nothing is deleted.
timeline.empty: No review of this run yet.
timeline.loadError: Could not load the reviews of this run.

form.title: Record a review
form.reasonPlaceholder: What the grade got wrong, and what you looked at.
form.tokenHint: The server's write token (BENCH_WRITE_TOKEN). Kept in this tab only.
form.readOnly: This server runs in {{mode}} mode, which refuses reviews. Only a live run folder takes new reviews.
form.noAuth: There is no login. The reviewer name is what you type here, and the write token is the only guard.

badge.hint: These outcomes come from a person's review, not from the verifier. They are evidence level reviewed, never verified.
badge.noneApplied: Grade source reviewed, no review applied

gradeSource.label: Grades
gradeSource.latestHint: Each experiment's newest regrade, where it has a result for the run.
gradeSource.reviewedHint: The sealed grades with human reviews applied on top. Regrades are not applied.

runs.title: Human reviews
runs.description: Reviews of each arm's run. They apply only under grade source reviewed.
